topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional non-targeted cancer treatment modalities, their mechanisms of action, and their clinical limitations.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities and DNA Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss strategies that selectively target inherent cancer cell vulnerabilities such as hormone dependency, cell-cycle checkpoint failure, and defective DNA repair.

topics.label: Targeted Kinase Inhibitors and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on the application of kinase inhibitors to target oncogene-driven signaling pathways and the molecular mechanisms underlying acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Targeted Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the use of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to specifically recognize tumor antigens and eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunology and Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system interacts with tumors and how therapeutic interventions like checkpoint blockade, BiTEs, and CAR T cells reactivate anti-tumor immunity.

topics.label: Overarching Challenges, Progress, and Future Directions in Oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the broader challenges in cancer treatment, historical improvements in patient survival, and emerging directions in oncology.
